title: Reverse a Stack
statement:
A stack contains `n` integers. You are given its contents listed from the **bottom** of the stack to the **top**.

Reverse the stack so that the element that was on top ends up at the bottom, the element that was at the bottom ends up on top, and so on. Print the contents of the reversed stack, again from bottom to top.

Values may repeat. The intended way to solve it is to use only the usual stack operations (`push`, `pop`, `peek`, `isEmpty`) together with recursion or one extra stack, rather than indexing into the stack.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer asked for the time and space complexity of the solution. Compare the recursive solution that inserts each popped element at the bottom of the stack (O(n^2) time, O(n) call-stack space) with the one that uses an auxiliary stack or array (O(n) time, O(n) space).
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers: the stack from bottom to top.
outputFormat: Print the reversed stack from bottom to top, separated by single spaces.
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 5000 (so a recursive solution stays within the recursion limit)

examples.explanation: The top is 5, so after reversing, 5 is at the bottom and 1 is on top.
Reading the original from top to bottom gives 7 7 -3 10, which is the new bottom-to-top order.
A stack with one element is unchanged.

hints: If you pop every element into another stack, in what order do they come back out?
For a recursive version, pop the top, reverse the rest, then work out where the popped element must go.
The popped element must end up at the very bottom of the reversed rest: write a helper that inserts an element at the bottom of a stack.
